Earlier this month, when listening to the Cortex podcast, the topic of decision fatigue came up. If I remember correctly, the main context the topic was brought up in was the prevalence of decision fatigue when navigating through airports. I started thinking about whether or not I was visibly affected by this fatigue.

I think the only times I am relatively affected is during grocery shopping, where I usually take time on each item to decide whether or not I should buy it.

However, I'm not the type that I'd think would be affected by decision fatigue in any great way in most areas of my life. So, Voaters who make a lot of decisions throughout your days, have you ever noticed the effects of decision fatigue in your decision-making? Is it something you knowingly try to avoid if you could?
How do you know when decision fatigue affects you? Have you ever felt it?

Is it something you knowingly try to avoid if you could?

We often don't realize it but we're making small decisions all of the time - which sidewalk to cross to, if I should do something now or 5 minutes later, which NetFlix series out of hundreds should I watch next, etc. Work for example is much about decisions - otherwise they'd just have a computer do it for you. Compare modern life to the pace of life a thousand years ago - humans did not have enough time biologically to really adapt themselves to this frantic lifestyle, things were much simpler back then.

So to avoid it you should get out of the city and go somewhere quiet, or take a personal day or sabbatical, do some relaxing activity that allows your mind to wander like reading, etc. Decision fatigue is just like normal fatigue - something that happens everyday and needs to be kept in check to live a healthy life.
